processing-time trigger emits 8, 15, 15 · watermark trigger emits 15 · threshold for the fix: 81s
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · window [12:00, 12:02) = 19
A PROCESSING-TIME TRIGGER, EVERY 60s — WHAT WINDOW [12:00, 12:02) READS
fires at 12:01:00
events in the window that have arrived: ids 0,1
emits 8
fires at 12:02:00
events in the window that have arrived: ids 0,1,2
emits 15
fires at 12:03:00
events in the window that have arrived: ids 0,1,2
emits 15
fires at 12:04:00
events in the window that have arrived: ids 0,1,2
emits 15
fires at 12:05:00
events in the window that have arrived: ids 0,1,2,7
emits 19
fires at 12:06:00
events in the window that have arrived: ids 0,1,2,7
emits 19
The trigger fires on the CLOCK, so it emits whatever has arrived — 8, then 15, then 15, then 15, then 19, then 19.
It first reaches the right answer, 19, at 12:05:00 — and it has no way to know that firing was the right one.
Step 1/4 — a trigger is the thing that says "emit now"
A processing-time trigger is the simplest possible "when": fire every 60s. It is never blocked and never wrong about its own rule — and it emits
8, then 15, then 15. The right answer appears at 12:05:00, indistinguishable from the firings before it.
When — triggers, watermarks, and allowed lateness
processing-time trigger emits 8, 15, 15 · watermark trigger emits 15 · threshold for the fix: 81s
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · window [12:00, 12:02) = 19
THE EVENT-TIME TRIGGER — FIRE WHEN THE WATERMARK PASSES THE WINDOW END
the window ends at 12:02; the trigger waits for the watermark to pass it
after event id 0 (seen 12:00:02)
watermark none yet < 12:02 — hold
after event id 1 (seen 12:00:04)
watermark none yet < 12:02 — hold
after event id 2 (seen 12:01:33)
watermark 12:00:30 < 12:02 — hold
after event id 3 (seen 12:02:12)
watermark 12:01:10 < 12:02 — hold
after event id 4 (seen 12:04:06)
watermark 12:03:05 >= 12:02 — FIRE
It fires once, after event id 4 at 12:04:06, emitting 15 from ids 0, 1, 2.
That is a claim of COMPLETENESS, not of elapsed time — and it is wrong, because id 7 has not arrived. The claim and the error are the same event.
Step 2/4 — a watermark lets a trigger say "the window is COMPLETE"
This trigger waits for a reason rather than a clock: fire when the watermark passes 12:02. It fires exactly once, at 12:04:06, and emits 15.
Compare that with the previous step: fewer firings, a meaningful claim attached to each — and still 15 rather than 19, because the watermark was
wrong about completeness.
When — triggers, watermarks, and allowed lateness
processing-time trigger emits 8, 15, 15 · watermark trigger emits 15 · threshold for the fix: 81s
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · window [12:00, 12:02) = 19
EARLY · ON-TIME · LATE
three separate triggers on one window, each answering a different need
EARLY — every 60s before the watermark
speculative: 8, 15, 15 — fast and knowingly incomplete
ON-TIME — when the watermark passes 12:02
15 at 12:04:06 — the pipeline's best claim
LATE — once per straggler after that
19 at 12:04:40, when id 7 lands
These are not alternatives — a real pipeline fires all three on the SAME window, producing 3+ results for one answer.
Early serves a dashboard that wants something now; on-time serves a report; late serves correctness. One trigger cannot serve all three.
Step 3/4 — so a pipeline wants THREE triggers, not one
The reason "when" is a question rather than a setting: these three triggers serve three different consumers, and a window fires for all of them.
One window, several published results — which is exactly the situation the fourth question ("how") exists to make safe.
When — triggers, watermarks, and allowed lateness
processing-time trigger emits 8, 15, 15 · watermark trigger emits 15 · threshold for the fix: 81s
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · window [12:00, 12:02) = 19
ALLOWED LATENESS — GARBAGE COLLECTION FOR WINDOW STATE
one knob, and the exact value at which the answer changes
watermark when id 7 arrives
state survives while watermark < 12:02 + allowed
so allowed must exceed 80s
allowed lateness = 80s
state already dropped — id 7 discarded, 15 stands forever
allowed lateness = 81s
state still held — the late trigger fires and corrects to 19
The threshold is 81s — not id 7's 230s of skew, which is the number a reader would guess.
It is set by how far the WATERMARK had advanced, which jumped from 12:01:10 to 12:03:05 in one event. The knob is calibrated against the
watermark, not against the data.
Step 4/4 — and allowed lateness decides whether the fix ever lands
Allowed lateness is how long a window's state is kept after the watermark passes — it bounds memory, and it decides whether a straggler can still
change an answer. Here the threshold is exactly 81s: at 80s the correction is impossible and at 81s it happens. That number comes from the
watermark's jump, not from the 230s of skew.
